transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

In meetings I keep jumping in over people and cutting them off before I can stop myself. It's starting to really affect my relationships with my colleagues, and I need to figure out why I can't seem to control it.
Do you also have trouble sitting still or feeling constantly restless, or is it mainly interrupting and talking over people?

I definitely struggle with restlessness; it constantly feels like I have an internal motor running or like I've had too much caffeine. In meetings, I'm always bouncing my leg, clicking pens, or finding excuses to stand up because sitting still feels almost unbearable. Even at home, I can't just sit quietly to watch a movie with my wife without getting antsy and needing to move around.
Before age 12, did you already have these kinds of attention, impulsivity, or restlessness problems, and did they cause problems in more than one setting such as school, home, or work?

Yes, this actually goes all the way back to my childhood. Even in elementary school, my teachers were constantly moving my seat or sending notes home to my parents because I couldn't stay in my chair. I was always blurting out answers and talking over the other kids, no matter how many times I was told to wait my turn.
Do these symptoms cause problems in more than one area of your life, such as at work, at home, or in social situations?

Yes, it definitely affects both. At work, my interrupting and losing focus has strained relationships with my colleagues, and a board member recently warned me it's damaging my credibility. At home, it impacts my marriage because I can't even sit through a movie with my wife without constantly getting up, checking my phone, or talking over the dialogue.
Do you also have trouble with attention, like making careless mistakes, losing things, being easily distracted, or forgetting to finish tasks?

Yes, absolutely. I get easily distracted by the smallest things, like a phone lighting up, and during long meetings my mind completely drifts off after about fifteen or twenty minutes. I'm also incredibly forgetful—my assistant jokes I'd lose my head if it wasn't attached because I'm constantly walking out without folders or missing scheduled appointments.
Do these symptoms happen in several settings and have they been present since childhood, or did they start only as an adult?

They have definitely been around since childhood, starting back in elementary school where my teachers constantly sent notes home because I couldn't sit still or wait my turn. And yes, it happens in multiple settings—not just in my board meetings at work, but also at home when I'm trying to relax and watch a movie with my wife.

Have these symptoms mostly caused problems with inattention and distractibility, or do you also have clear hyperactive-impulsive behaviors like frequent fidgeting, leaving your seat, blurting out answers, and interrupting people across many situations?

While I do experience some distractibility, the hyperactive-impulsive behaviors are definitely the most prominent and occur across all areas of my life. I'm constantly fidgeting by bouncing my leg or clicking pens, struggling to stay in my seat, and blurting things out or interrupting people. This happens at home too, where that constant "motor running" feeling makes it impossible to even sit quietly through a movie with my wife.
Did these hyperactive and impulsive symptoms start before age 12 and cause problems in more than one setting, such as at school, home, and work?

Yes, they definitely started before age 12; in elementary school, teachers constantly sent notes home because I couldn't stay in my chair and kept blurting out answers. Today, it still impacts me in multiple areas, leading to a warning from a board member at work and making it impossible to sit quietly through a movie with my wife at home.
Have these symptoms been present continuously for at least the past 6 months?

Yes, they have been present for much longer than six months. They've been particularly disruptive for about a year and a half now, ever since I transitioned into my current operations role, and they have remained constant despite my best efforts to manage them.

Have you ever had a period when these symptoms started or got much worse after using caffeine, stimulants, recreational drugs, or a new medication, or when you had a medical problem like thyroid disease?
No, I don't think any of those are triggers for me. I don't use recreational drugs, I'm not on any new medications, and as far as I know, I don't have thyroid disease or any other medical issues.
Have these symptoms caused significant problems in your work, home, or social life, and have you ever had a period when they were much better or absent?

Yes, they've caused significant problems—my behavior has led to colleagues avoiding involving me in discussions, a board member warning me about my credibility, and at home, I can't even sit through a movie with my wife. While I've had these tendencies since childhood, they became highly disruptive and constant about a year and a half ago when I transitioned into my current operations role, and they haven't improved since.

Did you have these attention or behavior problems in more than one setting as a child, and did teachers or parents ever describe you as unusually inattentive, hyperactive, or impulsive compared with other children?

Yes, definitely. During elementary school, my teachers frequently moved my seat and sent notes home to my parents because I couldn't stay in my chair. They always described me as disruptive because I would blurt out answers and talk over the other children instead of waiting my turn.
Were you also having similar problems with attention, impulsivity, or restlessness before age 12 at home and in school, and did they cause noticeable problems in both places?

Yes, they definitely go back to my childhood and caused issues in both places. Even in elementary school, my teachers frequently had to move my seat or send notes home to my parents because I couldn't stay in my chair, constantly blurted out answers, and talked over other kids despite being told to wait my turn.
Did these attention, impulsivity, or restlessness problems clearly begin before age 12 and cause noticeable problems both at school and at home?

Yes, they definitely started back when I was in elementary school. My teachers frequently moved my seat or sent notes home to my parents because I couldn't stay in my chair, blurted out answers, and constantly talked over the other kids instead of waiting my turn.
Have you ever had a period of several days or more when you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep, and were more talkative or impulsive than usual?

No, I've never experienced distinct periods of feeling unusually euphoric or needing significantly less sleep. My restlessness and talkativeness are more of a constant, daily struggle that I deal with every single day rather than something that comes in episodes.
Do you also have ongoing trouble with inattention, like making careless mistakes, losing things, or being easily distracted, even when you are not feeling restless?

Yes, absolutely. My mind frequently drifts off in meetings after 15 or 20 minutes, and I'm easily distracted by small things like a phone lighting up or someone shifting in their chair. I'm also incredibly forgetful, often leaving folders behind or missing calendar appointments, to the point where my assistant jokes I'd lose my head if it wasn't attached.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for ADHD with prominent combined inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms, with the hyperactive-impulsive features most prominent. Symptoms began in childhood before age 12, occur in multiple settings (work and home, with childhood school impairment), have persisted for well over 6 months, and cause clear functional impairment. No evidence was elicited for episodic mania, substance/medication-induced symptoms, or a medical cause.
